plan.summary: Add JS/TS symbol extraction with tree-sitter while preserving Python byte-identical output and safe fallback behavior.

steps.action: Implement repo helper changes in mirofish_lab/repo.py: add _LANG_PARSERS, dispatch extract_symbols() by suffix, add js_symbols()/ts_symbols(), and introduce source_files(langs=...) while keeping python_files() as a compatibility shim.
steps.rollback: restore the previous repo.py helper implementations and the original python_files() behavior
steps.observability: Verify .py extraction remains byte-identical via existing golden/sample report checks and that old call sites still resolve

steps.action: Add optional tree-sitter dependencies to requirements.txt for tree-sitter, tree-sitter-python, tree-sitter-javascript, and tree-sitter-typescript.
steps.observability: Track pip install success across supported environments and confirm no new install-time failures

steps.action: Wire tree-sitter import handling in repo.py so JS/TS parsing uses it when available, but falls back to no symbols with a clear warning when import/grammar loading fails.
steps.rollback: disable the JS/TS parsing path and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Watch parser import failures, warning log coverage, and confirm JS/TS inputs degrade to no-symbols instead of crashing

steps.action: Run regression validation on existing Python repos to prove extract_symbols() and sample report output remain byte-identical after the dispatch change.
steps.rollback: revert the symbol-extraction change for .py files to the prior ast.parse path
steps.observability: Compare Python symbol diffs against baseline and confirm reports/sample.md reproducibility is unchanged

steps.action: Add/refresh audit logging for parser fallback and symbol-extraction failures so JS/TS no-symbol cases are traceable.
steps.rollback: disable JS/TS extraction path and redeploy_previous
steps.observability: Check logs for fallback events, parser failures, and coverage of emitted warnings

steps.action: Prepare the user-facing release note/changelog entry and support guidance describing JS/TS support and no-symbol fallback behavior.
steps.rollback: remove the release-note entry and send a correction notice
steps.observability: Confirm approved customer messaging and support runbook updates are published

steps.action: Obtain security review approval for the new tree-sitter dependency set before release.
steps.observability: Track security review decision and any dependency concerns

steps.action: Get API compatibility approval for the helper rename/shim so existing CLI consumers keep working without signature changes.
steps.rollback: restore python_files() wrapper and previous call signatures
steps.observability: Verify internal callers still work with the compatibility shim

steps.action: Secure named customer escalation ownership for the rollout period.
steps.rollback: reassign escalations back to the previous owner
steps.observability: Confirm escalation contact is assigned and published internally

steps.action: Wait for required release timing windows: business-hours-only, outside incident/launch windows, not Friday afternoon, and after-hours only if any schema-related work is later introduced.
steps.rollback: postpone deployment and keep previous version active
steps.observability: Confirm rollout timing satisfies all required change windows and no incident/launch window overlaps exist

steps.action: Deploy the code and dependency changes with the JS/TS extraction feature flag disabled by default, preserving Python-only behavior until approval to enable.
steps.rollback: disable the JS/TS extraction flag without redeploy
steps.observability: Watch deployment health, import errors, and confirm Python behavior stays unchanged post-deploy

steps.action: Enable JS/TS extraction on a limited set of representative repositories and backfill in small batches to avoid IOPS spikes.
steps.rollback: pause backfill and resume with a smaller batch size after lag returns to baseline
steps.observability: Track replication lag, indexing throughput, and diff-to-symbol mapping correctness on JS/TS repos

steps.action: Maintain a 24-hour clean burn-in on representative JS/TS repositories before broadening rollout.
steps.rollback: turn off JS/TS parsing flag and fall back to no-symbols path
steps.observability: Watch error rates, fallback frequency, and any parser regressions during the burn-in period

open_questions: Which release-owner and API owner will provide the required approvals?
Who is the named customer escalations owner?
What representative JS/TS repositories should be used for the limited rollout and burn-in?
Is there any actual schema work involved, or can the after-hours schema window be considered not applicable?
Can the legacy python_files() wrapper remain indefinitely, or should it eventually be retired after the quiet-period constraint is satisfied?

conflicts.issue: One stakeholder requires a 7-day quiet period before dropping legacy source-file handling, while another wants a compatibility shim for old python_files() callers. Resolved conservatively by keeping a python_files() shim and not retiring legacy handling in this plan.

JS/TS support depends on adding tree-sitter dependencies, but security requires review before shipping them. Resolved by sequencing dependency installation before code reliance and gating release on security approval.

Rollout requires business-hour/quiet timing and avoiding launch windows, while customer comms require advance notice. Resolved by placing comms and approvals before deployment and deferring launch to a compliant window.
